problem: VLN agents in long-horizon tasks suffer from planning/memory deficits and lack predictive foresight; language-CoT VLM planners and latent world models are developed separately, causing semantic hallucination in plans or semantic drift in predictions.
motivation: Humans navigate hierarchically via milestones and anticipate what they will see. A single VLM that both plans in language and imagines future geometric/semantic features could keep plans grounded in visual reality and predictions tied to the instruction, without expensive pixel generation or action-conditioned trajectory sampling.
key_idea: Train one Qwen2.5-VL-3B to output hierarchical language plans (summary, next sub-instruction, action) and, through learnable dream queries, predict short-horizon and milestone-horizon depth/DINOv2/SAM features that condition an MLP waypoint policy.
insight: Ablation (Table 2) shows VLM planning is the largest contributor (SR 66.2 vs 48.8 without it), and long-term milestone prediction adds further gains (SR 58.6 without it vs 66.2). Both depth and semantics predictions help, with semantics slightly more (SR 60.0 without semantics vs 61.8 without depth). The short-term horizon must match the waypoint length (k=5 best). Predictions beat identity baselines only at short horizons, yet semantic foresight matters more than geometric precision.
method: Hierarchical planning dataset: Gemini 2.5 Pro decomposes R2R-CE/RxR-CE instructions into sub-instructions and milestone keyframes; each sampled waypoint gets a navigation summary, future plan and language action; ~1.3M RxR-CE + 0.2M R2R-CE samples, rebalanced for straight/stop.
Unified VLM backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct trained autoregressively on plans, interleaved with world-model/action data; a position encoder embeds relative pose of each frame; ViT frozen.

Dual-horizon dream queries: learnable short-term (fixed k=5 steps) and long-term (adaptive horizon to next milestone) queries, each with depth, DINOv2 and SAM subqueries (64 tokens each, six subsets), decoded by 2-layer ViT decoders (VQ-VAE decoder renders depth).
Structured attention mask: long-term queries attend to short-term ones; depth and semantic queries masked from each other; a single action query attends to everything.
Predictive action policy: action embedding processed by a 2-layer transformer with dream embeddings and an MLP head outputs K=5 waypoints (x,y,sin,cos) plus arrival flag.
Loss: L = 0.25*SiLog depth + 0.3*MSE semantics + MSE action; 3 epochs on 64 H20 GPUs.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (fine-tuned) with lightweight decoders and MLP action head
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE public training episodes only, plus Gemini 2.5 Pro-generated hierarchical planning labels (~1.5M samples); precomputed depth, DINOv2, SAM features
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (history up to 20 frames) plus relative pose; no depth input or odometry listed in table
setting.action_space: predicted continuous waypoints (K=5, x,y,sin,cos) with stop flag
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth/DINO/SAM targets used only as training supervision)

results: On R2R-CE val-unseen NavForesee gets SR 66.2, OSR 78.4, NE 3.94, SPL 59.7, beating CorrectNav (SR 65.1, NE 4.24, OS 67.5) on SR/NE/OSR but with lower SPL (59.7 vs 62.3). On RxR-CE it gets SR 66.3 / SPL 53.2, slightly below CorrectNav (69.3 / 63.3).
limitations: Weaker on RxR-CE (SR 66.3, SPL 53.2 vs CorrectNav 69.3/63.3), and lower SPL than CorrectNav on R2R-CE; trained only on R2R-CE/RxR-CE, limited generalization.
Long-term predictions degrade because milestone locations are unknown at inference and tend to track short-term outputs; predictions beat identity baselines only up to T+2 (depth) / T+3 (DINO).
Depends on Gemini-generated plan labels and pixel-supervised depth predictions that are coarse; no real-robot validation.
